evidenceBoundary: Real locally installed Chromium-family browser sessions against loopback fixtures, deterministic scripted-provider server wiring, and inspection of the existing desktop app.asar. No live web research or live cloud inference was invoked.
problemRecovered: A failed navigation that created an implicit tab left that tab allocated. A failed explicit-tab navigation could still be racing Chromium's chrome-error navigation, preventing immediate retry on the same tab id.

change.implicitFailure: A newly created tab is closed when its first navigation fails.
change.explicitFailure: A failed explicit tab replaces its underlying page with a fresh page while retaining the tab id, then returns BROWSER_NAVIGATION_FAILED. The caller can retry on that id immediately.
change.safety: URL policy, request-level redirect checks, isolated profiles, secret redaction, download quarantine, and autonomous external-write denial remain unchanged.

proven: The governed browser runtime can drive an installed Chromium-family browser through local navigation, multi-tab research, inspection, interaction, screenshot, and verification paths.
Failed navigation no longer leaks an implicit tab and an explicit tab is immediately reusable under the same tab id.
The existing packaged app contains the governed browser runtime, tool executor, and verifier modules and passes the BrowserWindow security audit.
Browser external tools remain wired through the server's governed external-tool surface and protected by permission/authority tests.
notProven: The new navigation-recovery change in a freshly rebuilt or signed desktop artifact; the inspected app.asar predates this source change.
Live public-web research quality, provider-driven browser tool choice, or browser-assisted engineering completion rate.
A visible end-user browser workbench or packaged UI activity display beyond the existing security boundary.
requiredNextEvidence: Build a new local desktop artifact in a separate output location, audit that artifact, and perform a user-visible browser-workbench smoke test. Live proof requires paired free-route tasks with identical repositories, budgets, and verifiers, recording browser receipts and external-route failures.
